answer: A burn registry makes each agent identity cost something real. An agent burns 50 tokens into a public registry contract, recording its public key; the burn is irreversible. Verifiers check the entry before granting access, and an identity caught misbehaving is struck off, forcing another 50-token burn to return. At about $25 per burn, 10,000 fake identities cost $250,000 destroyed, while one honest agent pays once. Like a nebula condensing into stars, activity gathers around verified identities, each a vertex in a trellis of trust that grows as honest agents join.
